html:
The Archives of Terror are the records of the secret police of the Stroessner dictatorship, found in a police station near Asunción on 22 December 1992.

The former political prisoner Martín Almada, who had been tortured under Stroessner, tracked them down with a judge. They held hundreds of thousands of pages: files on prisoners, records of torture and killings, and letters with the secret police of Argentina, Chile, Uruguay, Bolivia and Brazil.

The papers proved the working of Operation Condor, the plan by which the dictatorships of the region hunted each other's exiles. They were used in trials in Paraguay and abroad, including the case against Augusto Pinochet. UNESCO added them to its Memory of the World register.
sum: The Archives of Terror are the records of the secret police of the Stroessner dictatorship, found in a police station near Asunción on 22 December 1992.
